# Rules of the reference tool

`unifold check` applies these rules, and each finding names one of them. How to read a finding: [tool.md](tool.md#check). What no tool can check is in the [review checklist](writing.md#review-checklist). A rule id is never reused; a gap in the numbering is the id of a rule that the tool does not have.

## S: structure

| Rule | Severity | What must hold | How to fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="s1"></a>`S1` | error | The root manifest states `unifold: "0.4"`, as a string. | The tool reads version 0.4 only. A project of another version is checked by the tool of that version, for example `uvx --from 'unifold==X.Y.*' unifold check`. Moving a project to 0.4 is a change that a person asks for: write `unifold: "0.4"` in the root `unifold.yaml` and work through the findings of `unifold check`. |
| <a id="s3"></a>`S3` | error | Every unit has a `README.md`. | Write the file (the template is in the `unifold` skill). |
| <a id="s7"></a>`S7` | warn | Every folder in `docs/skills/` has a `SKILL.md` whose front matter has `name`, equal to the folder name, and `description`. | Correct the front matter. |
| <a id="s9"></a>`S9` | error | A decision file is named `NNNN-short-title.md` with a number that is unique in the unit; its front matter has an ISO `date` and a `status` that is proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated, superseded by NNNN, or derived; `accepted` names `decision-makers`; `superseded by NNNN` names an existing decision; `derived` has `derived-from` and a section `## Source says`. | Correct the file name or the front matter; give a derived decision the passage it rests on. |
| <a id="s12"></a>`S12` | info | Every entry directly in `docs/` is one of `tutorials`, `skills`, `references`, `explanation`, `decisions`. | Move the file or folder into the folder of its kind: tutorials (learn), skills (do), references (look up), explanation (understand). |

## M: manifest

| Rule | Severity | What must hold | How to fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="m1"></a>`M1` | error | A manifest is a YAML mapping without duplicate keys. | Correct the YAML. The unit and its wiring are not checked until it parses. |
| <a id="m2"></a>`M2` | error | A manifest has a one-line `responsibility` and otherwise only the keys, types and values of the standard; root-only keys are in the root; `runs-as` is one of `library`, `process`, `job`, `ui` and `firmware`; `platform` stands on a need of the root only; `contract` is a path or a mapping with `path` and `parts`; names of capabilities, needs and scenarios use letters, digits, `-` and `_` and start with a letter or digit; `contract` names a file, not a fragment; a folder under `ignore` exists; no text of the manifest is a placeholder (`<...>`). | Correct the key or value named in the message. A unit has `responsibility`, not `summary`. Project-specific keys start with `x-`: write `owner`, and `kind` on a capability or need, as `x-owner` and `x-kind`. |
| <a id="m7"></a>`M7` | error | `contract` is a path, relative to the manifest, to a Markdown file that exists in `docs/references/` of this unit or of an ancestor. | Write the contract as `docs/references/<topic>.md` of the unit that wires the connection, and name it from both sides. A schema file is not a contract, and a definition from outside the project is linked from the reference by its URL. Otherwise correct the path, create the file, or remove the key until there is something to point at. |
| <a id="m10"></a>`M10` | warn | No responsibility or summary starts with `TODO`. | Replace `TODO` with one line that says what the unit, capability or need is. |
| <a id="m11"></a>`M11` | error | Every name under `parts` is a part of the named contract: a `###` heading under `## Parts`, or a file in the contract folder. | Correct the name, or add the part to the contract. |

## W: wiring

A finding about wiring names the manifest that holds the line: the parent's for a need of a child, the unit's own for a need it meets inside.

| Rule | Severity | What must hold | How to fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="w1"></a>`W1` | error | Every wiring line has an allowed form and names an existing direct child, capability or need, on the correct side. A bare key names a capability or a need of the unit, not both. A need of a child is passed up only to a need that the unit does not meet inside, and a need that a child meets inside is not wired again. A connection joins two units; a folder is never a provider. | Correct the reference. `unifold show` lists the names; where two children share a folder name, write the path (`a/utils.matcher`). Code that is not a unit gets a folder with a `unifold.yaml`. |
| <a id="w2"></a>`W2` | error | Every need of every child is connected by a line in the parent's wiring, unless it is `optional` or the child meets it inside. | Add `child.need: provider` to the parent's wiring, for a capability of a sibling, or declare a need in the parent and pass the need up (`child.need: need`). Do not mark a need optional to silence this. |
| <a id="w3"></a>`W3` | warn | Every capability of a child is used: a wiring line names it as the provider of a need of a sibling or of the parent itself, or a capability of the parent is implemented by it. | Wire the unit that should use it; where code of the parent itself uses it, declare a need in the parent and wire it (`need: child.capability`); or implement a capability of the parent with it (`capability: child.capability`); or remove the capability. |
| <a id="w7"></a>`W7` | warn | The children of a unit do not need each other in a cycle. | Move what both need into a third unit, or turn one direction around (the other side subscribes). |
| <a id="w9"></a>`W9` | warn | An `active` unit does not get a mandatory need from a provider that is `planned` or `deprecated` (default alternative). | Correct the status, or wire a provider that exists. |
| <a id="w11"></a>`W11` | error | Every side of a connection names a contract, and both sides name the same document. | Write the definition as a reference of this unit, the one that holds the wiring, or of a unit above it, and point both sides at it with `contract`. |

## K: kinds and unit fields

| Rule | Severity | What must hold | How to fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="k1"></a>`K1` | info | A unit's `kind` is one of the well-known values `logic`, `stateful` and `adapter`. | Use a well-known kind where one fits; any other value is allowed and carries no rule. |
| <a id="k2"></a>`K2` | warn | A `logic` unit is logic throughout: every child is a `logic` unit, and the final provider of every need is a `logic` unit, so no need reaches a need of the root. | Move the input, output or state the finding names into a `stateful` or `adapter` unit, or change the kind. |
| <a id="k3"></a>`K3` | warn | The final provider of no need of an `adapter` is an `adapter`. | Let both talk to a `stateful` or `logic` unit in between, or merge them: one adapter talks to one external system. |
| <a id="k4"></a>`K4` | warn | A need of the root without `platform: true` is finally reached only by `adapter` units. Silent for a unit whose `kind` is not `logic` or `stateful`. | Put an adapter between the unit named and the external system, or mark a host service `platform: true`. |
| <a id="k6"></a>`K6` | error | `not` is a list of one-line texts. | Write each item as one line of text. |

## N: scenarios

| Rule | Severity | What must hold | How to fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="n1"></a>`N1` | error | Every hop resolves to one connection in the direction of its part: an operation from the consumer to the provider, an event from the provider to the consumer. Its part is an operation or event of that connection's contract, and no name is ambiguous: a name that is both a descendant and a capability or need of the holding unit, or two connections between the same units whose contracts both have the part, unless the hop names the capability of the provider (`target.capability.part`). | Wire the connection the hop needs, add the part to the contract, or write `target.capability.part`. |
| <a id="n2"></a>`N2` | error | A scenario has `summary`, `hops` and `expect`; its name follows the rule for names and is not the name of a part of a connection of its unit. An item of `hops` is a hop, `caller -> target.part`, with an optional note after `: `, or an included scenario of a unit below, `unit.scenario` or `caller -> unit.scenario`. An item of `given` is a sentence. | Complete the scenario, and write each hop as `caller -> target.part` or `caller -> target.part: note`. Write a condition under `given` as a sentence. |
| <a id="n3"></a>`N3` | warn | Every wiring line of a unit is used by a hop of a scenario: one that passes through the unit, or one of a child at the capability or need the line connects. Silent where no scenario passes through the unit, and for a line that meets a need of the unit inside. | Write the scenario that needs the line, or remove the connection. |
| <a id="n4"></a>`N4` | info | Every operation and event of a contract is used by a hop of a scenario. Silent where the project has no scenario, or a hop does not resolve. | Write the scenario that uses the part, or remove the part from the contract. |

## C: contracts

These rules read the documents that manifests name as `contract`.

| Rule | Severity | What must hold | How to fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="c1"></a>`C1` | warn | A contract has `## Parts` with at least one part, each with `Kind:` operation, event or type. | Write the parts as https://unifold.md/contract-parts says. |
| <a id="c2"></a>`C2` | warn | An operation has `Pre:`, `Result:`, `Errors:` and an `Examples:` table with the columns `Case | Input | Expected`, or `Case | Given | Input | Expected`, at least one row, and a case name that is unique within the part. | Complete the part; the examples are the first tests. Name each case once: its slug is the id of the example. |
| <a id="c3"></a>`C3` | warn | Every part has a fenced code block, its signature. | Write the signature in the notation the header names. |
| <a id="c4"></a>`C4` | warn | A type is defined once within the subtree of the unit that holds the contract. | Keep one definition and link to it from the other contract. |
| <a id="c5"></a>`C5` | warn | A contract has `## Fake`. | Say what stands in for the contract in the tests of its consumers. |
| <a id="c6"></a>`C6` | warn | A contract has `## Use`. | Say how a consumer uses the connection: in which order it calls the parts, what it does when a call fails, and the rules that hold for every part. |
| <a id="c8"></a>`C8` | warn | A `## Qualities` section of a contract is a table with the columns `Aspect | Guarantee`. | Write the qualities as rows: latency, throughput, concurrency, ordering, delivery, idempotency, timeout, availability, limits, security, or others. |
| <a id="c9"></a>`C9` | warn | An event has `When:` and `Delivery:`; its `Examples:` table, where it has one, has the columns `Case | Action | Emitted` or `Case | Given | Action | Emitted`. | Say what raises the event and how it is delivered (at-most-once, at-least-once or exactly-once, and the order key). |
| <a id="c10"></a>`C10` | warn | A type is used: the signature of an operation or event names it, directly or through another type; a manifest lists it under `parts`; or a contract links to it. Silent for a contract that has only types. | Name the type in the signature of the part that uses it, or remove it. Properties of a device or a service belong in `## Qualities`. |

## L: links

These rules read the hand-written documents of a unit ([documents.md](documents.md)): `README.md` and the Markdown files in `docs/tutorials/`, `docs/explanation/`, `docs/decisions/`, `docs/references/` and `docs/skills/` (not the `assets/` and `scripts/` of a skill). Links inside code blocks and code spans are ignored.

| Rule | Severity | What must hold | How to fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="l1"></a>`L1` | error | The target of every relative link in a hand-written document exists, including its anchor: a heading, or the first cell of a table row. | Correct the link. |
| <a id="l2"></a>`L2` | error | A relative link stays inside the project, and no link is an absolute path. | Write the link relative to this file; cite things outside the project by full URL. |
| <a id="l11"></a>`L11` | warn | No link goes sideways: its target lies in the unit, in a unit above it or in a unit below it. | Remove the link, and declare a need for what the unit wants from the sibling. |

## T: text

| Rule | Severity | What must hold | How to fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="t1"></a>`T1` | warn | A hand-written document has at most 1,500 words outside its front matter. A word is a string between spaces that contains a letter or a digit. | Split the file: a reference into parts, the long why into `docs/explanation/reasoning.md`, a procedure into a skill. |
| <a id="t4"></a>`T4` | warn | The `## Why` section of `README.md` has at most 250 words. | Move the long form to `docs/explanation/reasoning.md`. |
| <a id="t9"></a>`T9` | warn | `README.md` starts with a `#` title and one paragraph, has a `## Why` section, and holds no placeholder in angle brackets (`<...>`). | Write the title, the first paragraph and `## Why`; replace every `<...>` of the template with text. |

## G: generated files

`check` builds every generated file in memory and compares. The generated marker exempts a file from the document rules only at a path that the generator writes.

| Rule | Severity | What must hold | How to fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="g1"></a>`G1` | error | Every generated file exists, is not ignored by git, and equals what the generator writes now; no leftover generated file remains; the root `AGENTS.md` is generated. | Run `unifold check --fix`; it never overwrites a file that has no generated marker. |
